     - Failing scenario: RFQ with two threads. Our sid is at `c_now > c_open` (the supplier raised its price). Every ask fails `cost <= min(c_open, c_now)`, and `closing_move` has no safe sheet to accept. The agent then sends a counter at `price <= theirs` that can still cost more than `c_open`, or that breaks a must-have inherited from the supplier's standing terms.
     - Suggested fix: in that branch, send the last sheet that passed the checks, or only an ask re-validated with `must_haves_ok`. Failing that, walk away or send a text-only message.
  
  2. **Timeout replies are counted as supplier concessions** (confidence.py:25-31, 86-87). `_sheets` takes every non-`buyer` message with a priced sheet, including the synthetic `from == "arena"` reply built in `play.py` `missed()`.

     - The cause is our slowness, not the supplier's floor. Suggested fix: exclude `from == "arena"` in `_sheets`, and consider dropping or lowering the timeout penalty.
  
  3. **A repeated supplier sheet looks like a zero concession** (confidence.py:35-42). If a supplier answers a question and re-sends the same standing sheet, the move is 0, which gives the -0.45 penalty. Suggested fix: skip a sheet whose terms equal the previous priced sheet, or compare by `term_sheet_id`.

  4. **Division by zero in `moves`** (confidence.py:38): `/ costs[0]` fails if the opening cost is 0. `limit` at line 78 can also be 0 if `round_limit` is 0. Neither is realistic, but a guard such as `max(costs[0], 1e-9)` is cheap. An `inf` cost would give `nan`, which `max/min` clamping would not clean up.

That accepts at a price still above what pushing might reach. This is a design risk, and it is safe only because of the `ok` and `c_open` guards.
  
  8. **`TONE_LOW` says "we are ready to close"** even when the agent is about to counter, which is the case whenever `c_now > c_open`. Consider whether that wording is intended.

  10. **Inherited `(done and left <= 1)` accept** skips the `c_now <= c_open` check. It is guarded by `ok`, but it can accept a price above `c_open`. This is SmartAgent behaviour and was left unchanged.

    - body tone selection;

Simulator results are in. `confident` beats `smart` on all three cases:

| Case | smart (v1-petra) | confident (v2) |
|---|---|---|
| S01 | 0.54 (€16.55) | **0.59** (€16.44) |
| S02 | 0.54 (€16.29) | **0.59** (€16.19) |
| S03 | 0.69 (€226.95) | **0.73** (€225.52) |

An honest reading of the logs: the simulator's supplier is a fixed script that concedes a set step and then agrees, so none of the "floor" signals (`final_offer`, shrinking concessions, wording) ever fired. Confidence stayed at 1.0 → 0.95 → 0.90, then hit 0.0 the moment the supplier said `agreed`, which triggered the early accept. The gain here came from the smaller step size (15% of the gap instead of 30%) while confidence was high — the agent held firmer, the supplier kept moving. Whether the back-off half of the index earns its keep can only be seen against the real suppliers, where `final_offer` and floor wording actually happen.

The reviewer is still checking the code. I'll report its findings and fix anything Critical before we wrap up.

The reviewer found no Critical issues, but three Major ones that would undermine exactly what you want the index for. Two of them make the agent *think* the supplier is at its floor when it isn't, which would trigger a premature accept:

1. **Our own timeouts count as supplier concessions.** A late reply from us makes the arena repeat the supplier's last sheet; the index reads that as a "zero move → near its floor" and after two timeouts it would early-accept mid-negotiation.
2. **A supplier re-sending the same sheet** (for example after answering a question) also reads as a zero concession.
3. **An inherited fallback in SmartAgent** can send an unvalidated sheet when nothing else is valid.

These are cheap to fix, so I'm sending them back to the coder along with the missing tests rather than shipping them.

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

input.message:
Code review came back: no Critical, but please fix these in the same files (still no git, no .env, smart.py stays untouched):

MAJOR 1 — `confident.py`, the `if not sheets:` fallback (inherited from smart.py): `sheets = [{"terms": complete_offer(case, {**terms, "unit_price": price})}]` is sent with no `must_haves_ok` and no `<= c_open` check. Fix in ConfidentAgent only: build that fallback offer, and only send it if `must_haves_ok(case, offer, std[sid])` and `cost(sid, offer) <= c_open`. If it fails, send a text-only message (no term sheets, body asking the supplier for a better package / cost breakdown) so we never send an unsafe sheet. Keep `closing_move` accept-if-possible before that, as now.

MAJOR 2 — `confidence.py` `_sheets`: synthetic timeout replies (`from == "arena"`, built by `RemoteTable.missed` in play.py; they repeat the supplier's previous terms) are counted as supplier sheets, so one of OUR timeouts registers as a 0-size "concession" and takes the -0.45 TINY_MOVE penalty on top of the -0.20 timeout penalty → after two timeouts conf≈0.15 → premature early accept. Fix: exclude `from == "arena"` messages from `_sheets` entirely. Also lower the per-timeout penalty to 0.10 (cap 0.30) and note in its comment that a timeout is our fault, not a floor signal.

MAJOR 3 — `confidence.py` concession: a supplier that re-sends the same standing sheet (e.g. answering a question) looks like a zero move → -0.45. Fix: in `_sheets`, drop a sheet whose `term_sheet_id` equals the previous kept sheet's id, or (if ids missing) whose `terms` dict equals the previous kept sheet's terms. Only genuine new sheets count as moves.

MINOR — guard division by zero / inf in `moves` (`costs[0]` could be 0 or inf): if `costs[0]` is not finite or <= 0, return no moves (concession part 0). Guard `round_limit` <= 0 in the rounds factor (treat as 1.0). In `FLOOR_PHRASES`, drop the standalone "withdraw" (matches "withdrawal") and drop "not possible" and "cannot go" (too common in polite non-final text) — keep the clearly final ones.

TESTS — add to `tests/test_confidence.py`:
- timeout reply (`from: "arena"`, same terms as previous supplier sheet) does NOT produce a concession penalty (parts["concession"] == 0) and the timeouts part is -0.10.
- a repeated supplier sheet (same term_sheet_id and terms) does not count as a zero move.

Done. The confidence index is implemented, reviewed, fixed and verified.

## Verdict on the idea

Good, with the two caveats from before: it is a heuristic over indirect signals (the supplier's floor is hidden), and it fixes the deal-loss risk, not the lever-finding problem behind our worst real scores (P03, P07). It is cheap, deterministic, and explainable per round, which suits both the 60-second limit and the jury.

## What was built (branch `v2-confidence`, nothing committed)

- `agent/arena_kit/confidence.py`: the index. Each turn it returns 0–1 plus a breakdown: `final_offer`/`agreed` hard-stop, shrinking supplier concessions, floor wording in the e-mail (English and German), contradicted data claims, our own timeouts, shrinking quote validity, rounds left.
- `agent/arena_kit/agents/confident.py`: `--agent confident`. SmartAgent with the index driving the concession step (15% of the gap at full confidence, up to 60% at zero), an early accept when confidence ≤ 0.25 and the standing offer is safe and beats the opening, and the e-mail tone (never a threat). All of v1-petra's safety checks stay. `smart.py` is byte-identical, so the backlog stays comparable.
- Review found no Critical issues. Three Major ones were fixed: our own timeouts and re-sent supplier sheets no longer look like "the supplier is at its floor", and the fallback path can never send an unsafe term sheet.
- 55 tests pass, lint clean.

## Results on the simulator

| Case | smart (v1-petra) | confident (v2) |
|---|---|---|
| S01 | 0.54 | **0.59** |
| S02 | 0.54 | **0.59** |
| S03 | 0.69 | **0.73** |

The simulator's supplier never hits a floor, so these gains come from holding firmer while confidence is high. The back-off half only shows its value against the real suppliers, where `final_offer` and floor wording actually occur. That needs the team key, which Niko holds: `uv run arena play case:P01 --agent confident -v`, then compare with the house agent's 0.97 on P01.

## What I need from you

1. **Commit and push?** I'd commit on `v2-confidence` and open a PR into `main`. Say the word.
2. **Backlog rows:** the team rule wants `version` as `v<N> - <name>`. I'd add the three simulator runs as `v2 - alex`. OK, or a different name?
3. **Real arena run:** whoever has the key should run `confident` on P01, P03 and P07 and read the replays. The log prints the confidence and its reasons every round, so you can see whether the index tracked what the supplier actually did.
